humanity.

2 weeks ago, Japan completed its 2-year term as a non-permanent member of the Security Council, and we renewed our strong determination to contribute to international peace and security even as we see crises in the conflicts in Northeast Asia, the Middle East, Ukraine, Africa, and elsewhere where the United Nations take a critical role, particularly in this year of the 80th anniversary of its founding. We must find ways to address these crises through strengthening the functions of the UN and protecting the fundamental principles of multilateralism, including respect for human dignity and rule of law. Mr. President, the Pact for the Future and its annexes, the Global Digital Compact and the Declaration on Future Generations are very meaningful leaders' level achievements on the goals that the United Nations should pursue towards a better future. This includes commitments on sustainable development, financing, science, technology, and innovation, as well as recommendations for reforming global governance, in particular referring to a need for urgent reform of the Security Council. Building on this significant momentum, we are determined to work even harder to realize a Security Council that better reflects the current global situation. The same is true for our commitment to achieving the SDGs by 2030. Japan will work to accelerate its efforts through the human security approach. This year, the 80th anniversary of founding of the UN coincides with the 80th year since the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. As the only country to have ever suffered atomic bombings during war, Japan has a historic mission to lead international efforts to realize a world without nuclear weapons. I would like to take this opportunity to reaffirm our unwavering resolve to promote nuclear disarmament and nonproliferation, and to make realistic and practical efforts to this end, especially through maintaining and strengthening the NPT regime. Mr. President, it entirely hinges on each member state whether the U.N. can regain is trusted or not, and each of us should thoroughly think how to rebuild our own UN in a more effective and meaningful manner. Japan will spare no effort to engage ourselves constructively to contribute to furthering these discussions. I thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Japan. I now give the floor to distinguished representative of Kenya.

Mr. President, Mr. Secretary-General, Excellencies, Kenya aligns itself with the statements delivered by the representatives of Iraq on behalf of the Group of 77 and China, and Djibouti on behalf of the African Group. I would like to thank the Secretary-General for the comprehensive outline of his priorities. Kenya supports his steadfast leadership and vision. I will now underscore 6 points. First, Kenya recognizes the urgency of reforming the international financial architecture. We reiterate our strong support for changes in the global economic governance and financial safety nets. We will continue to advocate for debt relief, a fairer international tax cooperation and innovative financing mechanisms. Second, as a member of the SDG Stimulus Leaders Group, Kenya will support the Secretary-General's efforts for a reform of the multilateral development banks and addressing sovereign debt distress. Kenya will continue to actively engage in the work of the open-ended Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee towards a United Nations Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation. Third, the call for a fairer fight against climate change must be sustained. The Africa Climate Summit, which was held in Nairobi, Kenya in September 2023, resulted in the operationalization of the Africa Carbon Markets Initiative, an initiative that represents a unique pathway to mitigate climate change, enhance energy access, and create green jobs. Fourth, as a leading country in regional peace efforts, Kenya strongly supports the Secretary-General's New Agenda for Peace. We urge and support a stronger use We are grateful for the good offices of the Secretary-General and will continue to engage actively in the activities of the Peacebuilding Commission, especially as we prepare for the forthcoming Peacebuilding Architecture Review. Fifth, the urgency of enhanced collaboration between the United Nations and the African Union cannot be gainsaid, especially because African countries continue to face structural and economic challenges that impede development. We welcome your efforts to deepen this collaboration. Finally, Mr. President, Kenya supports the vision of fostering people-centered, inclusive, and development-oriented information and knowledge societies. We look forward to the World Summit on the Information Society WSIS+20 review later this year. We also support the Secretary-General's emphasis on the strengthening of the UN Resident Coordinator System. Kenya has benefited immensely from the integration and coherence provided by the UN country teams in mobilizing resources, strengthening disaster preparedness and building resilience. In conclusion, Kenya reaffirms its commitment to supporting the Secretary-General's priorities and working collaboratively with all partners to achieve our shared objectives for a more peaceful, sustainable, and equitable world. I thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of Kenya. Please, before giving the floor to the next speaker, I appeal to you, reduce your time of speaking to 1 minute only because we must stop, we must come to an end. Please respect the speakers after you, 1 minute, not more, so that we can hear everybody.

Thank you.

Thank you. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Lesotho.

Mr. President, the Kingdom of Lesotho joins others in welcoming the Secretary-General's trenchant report on the work of the organization and his priorities for the 79th session of the United Nations General Assembly. My delegation further commends the SG for his sterling work in the past year despite the unending geopolitical tensions and conflicts which continuously divert the United Nations' attention from the sustainable development trajectory to humanitarian and conflict interventions. With regard to the report, we hail and support the SG's efforts of continuously advocating for the reform of the international financial architecture to address the financial needs of developing countries, in particular the need to address the conditions of borrowing which are not favorable to undeveloped countries, as well as the need for representation at decision-making levels of these institutions. We regret to note from the report that progress on the implementation of SDGs and fight against climate change has been stalled by lack of sufficient financial support. In this regard, we wish to emphasize the importance of the forthcoming FFD4 Summit in June. Our hope is that Member States will take full advantage of this conference to agree on a set of actions needed to address financing challenges to accelerate actions to implement the 2030 Agenda. While we appreciate commitments made on the Doha Programme of Action for LDCs, we remain concerned that 2 years since its adoption, the report notes little progress in implementation commitments on the— of the commitments made. On the same token, as we begin the implementation phase of the new Programme of Action for LLDCs, we call on the SG's Office to ensure that the Resident Coordinators and Country Teams work together with National Focal Points in ensuring that these blueprint programmes of action are implemented at country levels. Mr. President, since the UN Charter places the responsibility for maintenance of international peace and security security solely in the hands of the Security Council, this body must discharge its functions with utmost firmness. In this regard, we advocate for greater attention to be on peacemaking and preventive diplomacy, as the cost of war is insurmountable. Lesotho recognizes that the UN has seen significant progress in promoting justice and international law in recent years, which is foundational to the UN Charter. However, ongoing efforts and a call for continued cooperation are still pivotal in upholding these important principles on the global stage. Thus, we firmly support the priorities with respect to strengthening accountability mechanisms, promoting peaceful dispute resolutions, environmental justice and sustainability, consolidating legal norms and global governance, and of course implementing the Pact for the Future and its annexes. I will stop here because of the time, Chairperson. Thank you.
Thank you very much, Lesotho, for being sensitive. I will now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Tunisia.

Thank you, President. First of all, my delegation would like to express its appreciation to the and his wide leadership of the work of the UN. Rest assured, you have our full support for your priorities for 2025. This new year is a new opportunity to achieve the conclusions of the Summit of the Future and the SDGs. We hope this new year will allow us to promote the goals of our organization and do everything we can to implement the conclusions of the Summit of the Future and address different challenges. We wish to underscore the following. Firstly, international law must be respected as well as resolutions from the UN. The root causes of marginalization and vulnerability around the world must be eradicated, and the gender dimension must be promoted in national policies as well as promoting and empowering women. Also, the commitment— collective commitments to solidarity and universal values must be promoted too, and the new agenda for peace must be supported. To conclude, we support the rights of the Palestinian people, particularly the inalienable and the imprescriptible right of the Palestinian peoples to create a state with Jerusalem, Quds Sharif, as its capital. Thank you very much.
I thank distinguished representative of Tunisia. I now give the floor to distinguished representative of Ukraine.

Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Secretary-General, we welcome briefing on your priorities for 2025. Delegation of Ukraine aligns itself with the statement delivered on behalf of the European Union And will make few remarks on national capacity. The effectiveness of the multilateral system hinges on our collective action to ensure that the United Nations, that is reaching its 80th anniversary, remains a strong and effective institution that upholds the principles of the UN Charter and international law in the first hand. This year will remain overburdened with global challenges and security threats, ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine as the gravest violation of the principles of the UN Charter is one of them. It continues to undermine international peace and security, global food and energy systems. It is crucial to continue to make full use of Secretary-General's mandate to address the threats and challenges stemming from this flagrant violation of the UN Charter, as well as to promote the vision of comprehensive, just, and lasting peace on the basis of the UN Charter principles. In February, we approached the 3rd anniversary of Russia's full invasion of Ukraine and 11th year of its ongoing aggression against our country. Due to the Russian Federation's expansion of the war against Ukraine, security in Europe and Indo-Pacific are now directly linked. The Russian Federation is fueling its aggression by acquiring weapons, including missiles, from other states, in particular the DPRK and Iran. In addition to acquiring arms from Pyongyang in violation of multiple Security Council resolution, it has taken a step towards a serious escalation and expansion of this war by enrollment of DPRK soldiers in its war against Ukraine. This dangerous development significantly escalates the risk and consequences of the aggression, destabilizing the region and undermining global security. Accountability for all violations of international law, including international humanitarian law, has to be ensured, and it is crucial to uphold comprehensive ongoing monitoring and reporting by all UN mechanisms and mandates. In this context, the role of the International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine is particularly important. We also count on impartial and credible monitoring and reporting of the human rights situation in Ukraine, encompassing all its temporarily occupied territories, as well as within the mandates of the UN Security Council regarding children and armed conflict and conflict-related sexual violence. To conclude, Ukraine is dedicated to work closely with you and will further support your efforts to contribute in building just peace and prosperity across the globe and to implement the Pact for the Future and 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, also as the candidate to the ECOSOC for 2026-2028. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Ukraine. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Italy.

Mr. Secretary-General, Mr. President, Italy aligns itself with the statement delivered by the European Union on behalf of its member states and would like to add some additional remarks in its national capacity. First of all, let me, Mr. Secretary-General, express my gratitude for your presentation of the report and for outlining your priorities for 2025. As we look towards 2025, Secretary-General, you can count on Italy's steadfast support in advancing the United Nations' work worldwide, beginning with the concrete implementation of the Pact for the Future and the Global Digital Compact. At the same time, it remains crucial to uphold the UN Charter amidst ongoing conflict and instability. As Russia's illegal, unjustified aggression of Ukraine continues to impact on global security, Italy calls for a ceasefire and peace talks for a just and lasting peace. In July this year, Italy will host the International Conference for Ukraine's Reconstruction, reaffirming our shared commitment for the country's future. The multifaceted tensions in the Middle East require a greater UN role and commitment— from Gaza to Lebanon to Syria— in order to advance inclusive and sustainable solutions. Human rights shall also continue being at the core of the UN agenda. 2025 will mark the 25th anniversary of the WPS Resolution and the 10th anniversary of the YPS Resolution. 2025 shall be the year of delivery for the 2030 Agenda. The forthcoming 4th International Conference on Financing for Development in Seville presents a unique opportunity to shape a renewed and more effective framework for financing sustainable development. Financing SDGs will eventually hinge on mobilizing and pooling together funds from all sources— domestic, international, public, and private. Italy is scaling up this approach, devoting key additional resources from different channels notably with a stronger focus on Africa. And finally, another key moment will be the UN Food Systems Summit+4, which aims to further assess global advancement in food systems transformation, reinforce political commitment, and accelerate action towards achieving SDG 2. Mr. Secretary-General, count on Italy's engagement to support you and your team in this endeavor. And I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Italy. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Ghana.

Thank you, Mr. President. At the outset, allow me to express gratitude to the Secretary-General for this— for his briefing today on his priorities for 2025 and for his able leadership of the Secretariat of the United Nations. The Secretary-General's priorities for 2025 remind us of our collective responsibility ability to reform, innovate, and unite in pursuit of a better world. The challenges before us are daunting, but they are not insurmountable. Ghana firmly believes that solidarity and cooperation are the cornerstones of meaningful progress. It is only through multilateralism that we can tackle systemic issues like global inequality and climate change. Ghana stands ready to work with all member states to constructively consider the Secretary-General's vision for 2025. Together, let us seize this moment to reshape our world, create a global financial system that is just, combat climate change with urgency and fairness, and ensure that no nation or individual is left behind. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Ghana. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Cameroon.

Thank you, President. I'd also like to thank the Secretary General for this morning's presentation. We are in an untenable situation because of the very nature, which is angry, and shows its anger through flooding, fires, and all sorts of disasters that we are no longer able to contain. Secondly, also because of the centrifugal forces that, thanks to human activity, we are developing, and they are creating hotspots of tension where there's war and open warfare. However, 2 things, President. We reached an agreement with a certain number of instruments which gave a source of hope. We were able to define together the future that we wanted. We also have defined the elements that this future needs in order to achieve the 17 SDGs. Together we have the will in the Paris Agreement, etc., shown this. So what's wrong then? Thank you, Mr. President. What's wrong is that for the time being there is not enough action. The implementation is not there. The political will is not there. So, we are sliding towards extremes. What we need to do now is to act together to reaffirm this political will that we need. Then we need to use the mechanisms that the UN has to be able to act in a tangible way, in a coordinated way, to implement what we've decided to do. We must particularly, above all, give the Secretary-General the means to overcome some of these obstacles and provide him with the financial means that he needs so that he isn't permanently facing a liquidity crisis. So what we need to do is to bring together all of the elements that we have identified as a springboard. Otherwise, as the Secretary-General said, we're on a one-way path to hell. Thank you very much. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Cameroon. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Algeria.

Mr. President, at the outset, I would like— at the outset, to express my sincere thanks and appreciation to you for wisely leading the work of the General Assembly. I would also like to thank His Excellency the Secretary-General for his comprehensive presentation of his priorities for 2025. In this regard, the delegation of Algeria commends the efforts by the UN to promote the objectives and purposes contained in its Charter to maintain international peace and security, achieve international cooperation and development, and make the organization the center of the work of all nations. As we are discussing the priorities of the new year, I would like to highlight the following. In relation to international peace and security, the geopolitical divisions have exacerbated conflicts, poverty, and food security, as well as insecurity and inequality. Yet we are full of hope that with your efforts we will achieve the most— more just and stable world. And here we would like to highlight the following. First, we commend the efforts to reach a ceasefire in Gaza and put an end to the immense suffering of the Palestinian people and to put an end to the occupation consistent with international law and relevant UN resolutions. To establish an independent sovereign state of Palestine with Jerusalem as its capital. In this connection, Algeria remains fully convinced in relation to the full membership of Palestine in our organization. Given the importance of the subject, Algeria being the president of the Security Council for this month, it has scheduled a high-level debate to discuss the situation in in Palestine on the 20th of the month. Second, more efforts should be made to enhance cooperation at the regional and international level to counter terrorism, in particular in Africa, to eliminate this threat and stem sources of its funding. Terrorism in Africa is the subject of an event organized by Algeria On the 21st of this month. We hope this meeting will produce outcomes and recommendations that will enable the organization to move ahead with countering terrorism. Third, the review of the peacebuilding architecture provides an opportunity to enhance the link between addressing the root causes of conflicts in relation to the lack of progress on the one hand and peace and security on the other. Fourth, coordination and action between the UN and the African Union should be promoted to ensure more strengthened cooperation to address the issues and support the African priorities in the implementation of 2030 Agenda and 2063 Agenda. And ensure the complementarity between the 2 agendas. Fifth, Security Council reform should be a priority to ensure the fair representation of the African continent and address the historic injustice it has suffered, as well as put the Iswilini Consensus and Sirte Declaration in the heart of the reform process. As to the socioeconomic and environmental aspect, we would like to highlight the following. The 4th Finance for Development Conference should produce outcomes that would help achieve the SDGs. Second, the Pact for the Future is a pillar to forge ahead with the programs and policies of sustainable development. And the Global Digital Compact should be used as a bridge to transfer the modern technology to the developing countries to develop their economies and narrow the gap between the North and South. Third, the gap between the North and South continues to be an impediment before the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals in an equal manner between all states. And while the South-South cooperation and trilateral cooperation are important aspects in international cooperation, they are not a substitute of the North-South cooperation, but they— it complements it. In conclusion, Mr. President, Algeria reiterates its support to actions for SDGs by cooperating with its partners to achieve the aspirations and hopes of our nations. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Algeria. I will now give the floor to the last speaker. That will be the distinguished representative from Angola. You have the floor, Angola.

Mr. President, Mr. Secretary-General, Excellencies, we thank the UN Secretary-General for presenting a comprehensive briefing on his priority for 2025. Angola aligns with the statement delivered by Iraq, Djibouti, and Brazil on behalf of G77, African Group, and CPLP respectively. The Secretary-General's priorities reflect the complex global scenario in which we live and reinforce the essential role of the United Nations in promoting peace, justice, human rights, and sustainable development. Angola acknowledges the progress achieved by the organization under the SEG's leadership. However, we also share the concern regarding the challenges outlined by the SEG in its priorities. It is crucial that multilateral efforts are intensified to address the challenges effectively and to ensure that no one is left behind. Mr. President, my delegation Commission also commends the Secretary-General's leadership for achieving gender balance in the senior management team. However, we encourage the same level of commitment to achieve balance in geographical representation in senior appointments at all levels of the Secretariat and in the field, including the appointment of the UN Resident Coordinators.
Thank you.

Mr. President, the Sustainable Development Goals are off track. More than 80% of the SDGs targets are at risk of not being met by 2030. With 5 years to go, we must accelerate action to fully implement the SDGs, especially in areas such as food security, health, education, and gender equality. Angola fully supports the Secretary-General's call for reforming the global financial architecture. It will allow developing countries to have fair and sustainable access to financial resources. This reform will also be essential to alleviate the debt burden of the most vulnerable countries and promoting the investment that ensures inclusive growth. Mr. President, the Security Council reform must remain a paramount priority. It should be more inclusive and more representative and address the historical injustice against Africa. In line with the Ezulwini Consensus and the SADC Declaration, the African continent still demands for 2 permanent seats and 3 additional non-permanent seat in the reformed Security Council. In addition, there is a growing consensus among member states that Africa's claims for the 2 permanent seats in the reformed Security Council should be treated as a special case. Africa cannot wait any longer. In the field of peace and security, Angola has positioned itself as an active mediator of regional conflicts. We will continue to support the UN in finding peaceful and sustainable solutions to existing conflicts, with special attention in the African continent. To conclude, as we prepare to assume the chairmanship of the African Union in February, Angola stands ready to work closely with the UN in our collective endeavor to build a fair, more inclusive, and sustainable future for all. We look forward to the PBC review and the upcoming resolution on UN-AU cooperation. We reaffirm the need to strengthen multilateralism. Only through the international cooperation and dialogue between nations, we will be able to tackle the global challenges affecting us all today. Thank you, Mr. President.

I thank the distinguished representative of Angola. I now invite the Secretary-General of the United Nations, His Excellency Antonio Guterres, to provide his observations on the interventions made by delegations.

Thank you very much, Mr. President. Let me first say that I am extremely grateful because we had today very important contributions to the perspective of solution of our problems and to the most important challenges that we are facing and the way to address them. And there was a very high level of consensus in this room today and this to a certain extent represents a paradox. and I believe that we need to face this paradox. On one hand, we have geopolitical divisions that have been deepening and that are the main reason why we see a multiplication of conflicts, creating the space— as the superpowers neutralize each other— creating the space for a number of spoilers to interfere with the different conflicts around the world, making them more difficult to be addressed and to be solved. But at the same time that we have these divisions, the truth is that the UN was able, in relation to some of the crucial challenges that we face— some of them existential the UN was able to come together in, I would say, a roadmap to solve many of the dramatic problems we face with the combination of the Agenda 2030 and the Pact of the Future and the 2 documents associated with the Pact of the Future. The Agenda 2030 defining a number of very clear objectives. It is the what is needed. Of course, we all witnessed that the agenda was not being implemented with the rhythm that was necessary, and that is the link with the Pact of the Future. The Pact of the Future is related to the how, to the mechanisms that are needed to accelerate the implementation of the Agenda 2030, and so we need to see these 2 documents together. And in relation to these 2 documents, there was a clear consensus that was again expressed in this session. And we will now have the opportunity to deal with the implementation of what was agreed. And I know that sometimes the implementation is the problem in the solution of many of our questions. We have that opportunity through a number of key moments where we will be discussing financing for development, the social dimension of development, where we will be discussing the rights of women and girls, where we will be discussing the oceans and their— the risks they are facing and their contribution to the global economy and the global society; when we will be discussing again climate, climate change and the way to address it effectively; when we will be discussing peacebuilding and a number of other aspects that will be the centre of a series of conferences that will take place in 2025. And what is absolutely essential is, on one hand, to make sure that we limit the impact of the geopolitical divisions in our peace and security situation. And fortunately, we are seeing beyond the spoilers that complicate problems a number of— a growing number of peacemakers, of countries that come to support the mediation efforts in order to solve conflicts, and we are seeing the first results of that mediation— what happened in Lebanon, what I hope will happen in Gaza. So we need to limit the impact of the geopolitical divisions on our peace and security dimension, and we need to avoid that these geopolitical divisions undermine the implementation of the Agenda 2030 and of the Pact of the Future and undermine the success of the different summits that we will be having in this year. And I truly believe that the consensus that was expressed in this meeting will help us bring everybody together to make sure that with all the dramatic challenges that we face when we open the Pandora's box, there are reasons to believe that the hope that stayed inside can materialize in the solution of many of the dramatic challenges that we face. Thank you very much for all of you for the excellent contribution that this meeting has represented.

I thank the Secretary-General of the United Nations. The informal meeting of the Plenary is now concluded. The resumed 56th Plenary Meeting will be held at 3 PM in this hall. The informal meeting is adjourned.

The meeting is resumed.
